title: Dual-feature selectivity enables bidirectional coding in visual cortical neurons.
summary: Macaque V1/V4 and mouse visual-cortex neurons showed dual-feature selectivity: elevated-baseline neurons were excited by preferred features and systematically suppressed by distinct non-preferred features, with graded responses across a continuum. Model predictions were tested against held-out images and recorded neuronal responses; reported selectivity patterns were cross-checked across models, macaque areas/species and mouse cortex. The authors note in-silico limitations, small animal counts, and lower V4 model coverage (52% retained).
ai_technology: Deep neural network functional digital twins predicted neuron responses to natural images, enabling systematic selectivity analysis over 1.2 million images and model-guided stimulus tests.

source_review.scope: Read the primary eLife full text (Methods and Results; PMC full text) and checked the Europe PMC record. The authors trained functional digital twins on macaque V1/V4 and mouse visual-cortex recordings, validated response predictions on held-out images and direct in-vivo responses, then screened 1.2 million natural images. They report that many neurons encode both preferred-stimulus excitation and systematic suppression by distinct non-preferred features, with the pattern also seen in mice and across cortical areas. First publication was 2026-11-09; the active and archived snapshots contain no exact matching DOI/title/result. The models provide the large-scale stimulus search; core recordings and cross-model/in-vivo checks support the result. Caveats: analyses rely substantially on in-silico responses, only two macaques per area, and high-confidence filtering retained 52% of V4 neurons.
